title: File Uploads
description: Learn how to handle file uploads in React forms.

data.text: File uploads are a special case in React because `<input type="file">` is an **uncontrolled** component — React cannot set its value for security reasons. Instead, you read the selected file from the DOM and send it to the server using FormData.
Access the selected file via `e.target.files`. This FileList contains File objects with metadata like name, size, and type.

data.title: Single File Upload

data.text: Add the `multiple` attribute to accept multiple files. Convert the FileList to an array with `Array.from()`.

data.title: Multiple File Upload

data.text: Use the native drag and drop API to let users drop files into a zone. Handle dragOver, dragLeave, and drop events.

data.title: Drag and Drop Zone

data.text: Always validate file type, size, and count on both client and server. Client validation improves UX; server validation is essential for security.

data.title: Validation Checklist
items: Check `file.type` against an allowlist (e.g., image/png, application/pdf).
Limit the number of files with `files.length`.
Show clear error messages for rejected files.

data.title: Never Trust the Client
data.text: Client-side validation can be bypassed. Always validate files again on the server before storing or processing them.

terms.definition: A browser API for constructing multipart/form-data requests, used for file uploads.
An input whose value is managed by the DOM, not React state.
A native browser API for accepting dragged files onto a drop zone.

data.caption: The file upload flow from selection to server.

data.title: Exercise: Image Uploader
data.description: Build an image uploader with preview and validation.
steps: Create an ImageUploader component with a file input and drag-and-drop zone.
Accept only image files under 2 MB.
Simulate an upload with setTimeout and show success or error.
data.expectedOutcome: An image uploader that validates files, shows a preview, and simulates server upload.

items.question: Why can't I control the file input value?
items.answer: Browsers block setting file input values for security. If JavaScript could set the file path, it could upload files without the user's knowledge.

items.question: What is the maximum file size I should allow?
items.answer: It depends on your server, but 5–10 MB is common for images. Check your hosting and CDN limits.

items.question: How do I upload files with additional fields?
items.answer: Append both files and text fields to the same FormData object before sending.

items.question: Can I upload files with fetch?
items.answer: Yes. Set method to POST and body to a FormData instance. Do not set Content-Type; the browser sets the multipart boundary automatically.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: File inputs are uncontrolled; read values from the DOM.
Use FormData to send files to the server.
Validate file type and size before uploading.
Drag and drop improves UX for file selection.
data.takeaway: File uploads are a special case in React, but with the right patterns they are straightforward to implement.
